questions.q: For a finite sequence $a=  \left(a_1, \cdots, a_n\right)$ of $n$ integers (where $n \geq 2$ ), define $S(a)=\sum_{\substack{i, j \in\{1,2, \ldots, n\} \\ i < j}} a_i a_j.$
options: For $a=  \left(a_1, \ldots, a_n\right)$ and $b=  \left(b_1, \ldots, b_m\right)$, define $a \star b=  \left(a_1, \cdots, a_n, b_1, \cdots, b_m\right)$. Then $S(a \star b)=S(a)+S(b).$

If $a$ is a sequence of $m+k$ integers with $m$ many 1 's and $k$ many -1 's then
$S(a)=\frac{m(m-1)}{2}+\frac{k(k-1)}{2}-m k.$
Then there is an integer $x$ such that for the finite sequence $a=(2,3, x, 2 x)$, $S(a)=-7$.
If $a$ is a sequence of 100 integers consisting of 2 's and -1 's only then the minimum possible value of $S(a)$ is less than -100.
